w: Swamishri arrived in London at 10.25 am (4.23 am American Standard Time) at Heathrow Airport and reached the mandir late due to heavy traffic at 1.10 pm. After performing puja, Swamishri blessed the audience and then retired to bed.

While Swamishri was having lunch, a sadhu was giving details about the Nobel Peace Prize. Swamishri was listening attentively. However, at the drone of conversation among the gathering Swamishri told everyone, "If anyone wants to get it then listen carefully."
The sadhus responded, "We are praying that you get the Peace Prize."
"Having got Akshar Deri; that is the biggest Nobel Prize," Swamishri responded. "There is no need to pray for that. We have already got it."
"We are all praying that you get the prize," a sadhu added.
"I have already got it - Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. So I do not have any wish at all. I am in Akshardham ..."
Swamishri's reply had striking ring of absolute fulfillment and attainment of the Divine.
One who desires more than one's requirements invites miseries.

A person performs two types of karmas. One he does with evil intentions. That is, when he gives pain to others, persecutes them, troubles them or creates difficulties, he regresses and attains hell. And if he devotes himself to God and performs good actions, then he will be elevated.
Perform your worldly duties but do not forget God. Engage yourself in bhajan while anchored to the refuge of God for it will give you happiness, peace and success.
Swamishri performed murti-pratishtha of the canvas murtis of Guru Parampara in the mandir sanctum.
After his morning puja Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha of murtis for hari mandirs in Acharda and Pandri villages (Surendranagar district and Limbdi sub-district respectively).

Guests : Hasan Kamal, Poet, Bahrain, praised, “Every column, every corner, every place made is really unique. It is hand made. A house takes more than two years to finish and this has been done in a very short period of time.”

Shri D.R. Kartikeyan, Former Director of CBI and Director General of Human Rights Commission, lauded, “If there is going to be an assessment on the 7 Wonders of the World, I think this complex is going to get the top most place. Every Indian should be proud of this. When you go around, it is just beautiful to look at and very entertaining. Every aspect of it imparts certain values of art and science of living a full life, harmonious life, spiritual life and a life full of harmony between various sects and groups of people all over the world.”
Abdul Hamid, Under Secretary, Bahrain, said, “Akshardham is so wonderful that it seems that aliens from another planet have come and made it. This is not a work of humans.”

Shri Balasubramaniam, Director of CBSE, praised, “I think it is a great spiritual monument which the city of Delhi should be proud of. It imbibes the basics of all religions, the immense wealth of our cultural heritage and the vibrancy of Indian thought. I think this kind of monument is required to make an impregnable impact on the younger generation of our country, who can really feel the mind and spirit of India.”

The annual gathering of past students who studied at the BAPS Gurukul in Gondal was held on the mandir grounds. More than 1,200 ex-students attended. The assembly commenced with reminiscences from past students. A drama, ‘Dream’, was enacted by the Gurukul boys. Then Mahant Swami gave awards to outstanding students of the Gurukul. This was followed by a traditional dance and offering of garlands to Swamishri. Another drama, ‘From Darkness to Light’, was performed by students of the Gurukul. Finally, Swamishri emphasized in his blessings about the need for values and understanding the glory of Yogiji Maharaj.

After the puja, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was coming to his residence. Meanwhile Balmukund Swami came down the slope all the way to the tamarind tree to meet Swamishri for darshan. Really, every day he comes once for Swamishri's darshan. Today he came all the way here to meet him. So Swamishri said, "You came all the way?!"
Balmukund Swami said, "Wherever you come, we must come to meet you, mustn't we!"
Swamishri said, "Wherever Yogibapa takes us, we must go."
A devotee phoned from America. He said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "I am troubling you, but please forgive me; I am very worried."
Swamishri said, "Do not worry about the trouble. We have no trouble; speak calmly."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was walking. Meanwhile the sadhus explained various verses of the Gita. In particular, they expounded in different ways the "Akshar Brahma Yoga" described in the Gita.
Finally Amrutswarup Swami asked, "Everyone has spoken about Aksharbrahma, but Bapa, who is this Aksharbrahma?"
After a short silence, Swamishri said, "Gunatitanand Swami is Aksharbrahma."
Amrutswarup Swami said, "But who is that Aksharbrahma now?"
Swamishri said, laughing, "They are all one and the same, aren't they!"
This was said and the walk ended. Panting a little, Swamishri said, "You have prepared very well. One realises how true Shastriji Maharaj's principle is."
Brahmmanan Swami said, "Please bless us that this principle becomes firm in our souls."
Swamishri said, "Keep faith and trust."
After the meal, during the reading of letters, Maheshbhai Patel of Richmond phoned from America.
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Tell me, Maheshbhai!"
Maheshbhai said, "Bapa! Don't call me Maheshbhai; call me Mahesh."
Swamishri said, "It's become a habit, hasn't it! So I said Maheshbhai."
Swamishri's courtesy gave everyone special inspiration.

After his puja, Pramukh Swami Maharaj was going back to his residence. Meanwhile, Balmukund Swami came down the slope all the way to the tamarind tree to meet Swamishri for darshan. He usually comes for Swamishri's darshan once every day. Today he had come all the way here to meet him. So Swamishri said, "You came all this way?!"
Balmukund Swami said, "Wherever you come, we have to come to meet you, don't we!"
Swamishri said, "We must go wherever Yogi Bapa takes us."
A devotee phoned from America. He said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "I am troubling you, please forgive me, but I am very troubled."
Swamishri said, "Do not worry about troubling me. It is no trouble for us. Speak calmly."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj was taking his walk. Meanwhile, the sants explained various verses of the Gita. In particular, they presented in different ways the "Aksharbrahma Yoga" described in the Gita.
At the end, Amrutswarup Swami asked, "Everyone has talked about Aksharbrahman, but Bapa, who is this Aksharbrahman?"
After a few moments of silence, Swamishri said, "Gunatitanand Swami is Aksharbrahman."
Amrutswarup Swami said, "But who is that Aksharbrahman now?"
Smiling, Swamishri said, "They are all one and the same, aren't they!"
With this the talk ended, and so did the walk. Panting a little, Swamishri said, "You have prepared very well. It shows how true Shastriji Maharaj's principle is."
Brahmamanan Swami said, "Please bless us so that this principle becomes firm in our souls."
Swamishri said, "Keep faith and trust."
After his meal, while Pramukh Swami Maharaj was reading letters, Maheshbhai Patel of Richmond phoned from America.
Swamishri said, "Tell me, Maheshbhai!"
Maheshbhai said, "Bapa! Please do not call me Maheshbhai, call me Mahesh."
Swamishri said, "It has become a habit, you see! That is why I said Maheshbhai."
Swamishri's courtesy gave everyone special inspiration.
Today, on the auspicious festival of Diwali, giving blessings after the morning puja, Mahant Swami Maharaj said:
"Brahmanand Swami sang, 'O Lord, for me every day is Diwali...' For one who has conviction, every day is Diwali. Without conviction, even the day of Diwali becomes Holi (a bonfire).

"Shastriji Maharaj showed great grace in giving us conviction. If Shastriji Maharaj had not been manifest, we would have been stumbling about somewhere! Other spiritual practices cannot match conviction. If there is conviction, all is well. Nothing remains.

"Maharaj says, 'I get on with those who have conviction.' Conviction is the 'one', the others are 'zeros'. The sum of a lakh zeros is only 'zero'. Conviction is the bridegroom. On the way to Chhapaiya, a Muslim wedding party was getting into Yogibapa's compartment. The bridegroom was small. He did not want to get in. So the others were forcing him into the compartment. The bridegroom said, 'I don't want to go... I don't want to go...' They explained to him, 'What will we do without you?' Conviction is in the place of the bridegroom. Without it, everything is useless! Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj and Pramukh Swami Maharaj have spread conviction, conviction, conviction on all sides. That is why we are happy. Whatever our condition, if we have conviction, then 'In this universe, consider anyone as fortunate as us, and that is your mistake...' So remain in strength; when this talk takes place, a lamp is lit within. On these five days we light lamps, so they stand apart from other days, but if a lamp is lit within...! Then if negative feelings and seeing faults go out, there is only light."
Thus, through his inspiring blessings, Swamishri lit lamps in everyone's heart.

ds.t: A New Year letter to all
w: Today, right after coming from his bath, Mahant Swami Maharaj expressed a wish: "I want to write a letter addressed to the whole satsang and spread it throughout the whole satsang."
Hearing this, the attendants requested, "How about writing it in the evening when you wake up?"
"No, let us write it now." Saying this, he at once sat down to write the letter. What was flowing in every particle of his being flowed through his pen onto the paper.
Here is that historic letter prasad of the New Year!
Swami Shriji
Param Pujya Pramukh Swami
Sakshat Sthan (the very place)
Gondal Akshar Deri
Sunday
To all sadhus, all volunteers,
all devotees, and all,
young and old,
Gift for Diwali and the New Year
Jai Shri Swaminarayan with much love from Sadhu Keshavjivandas.
There is no doubt that all of you sadhus and volunteers are increasing satsang through tireless effort. All of you are blessed.

Now, to spread satsang even more and for satsang to take root in ourselves, there is a great need for unity. In this, one thing must be understood: what is important is what we can do for unity. Let us not expect anything at all from the other side; if it comes, fine, but it is we who must keep unity. How should we think so that unity grows? What should we say so that unity grows? And let us dislike whatever lacks unity. Pramukh Swami Maharaj went so far as to say that we will have to keep unity even if it means swallowing poison. At the time of a terrible shortage of money, Yogibapa said, "We do not want money; we want unity."

These great souls lived it and showed us. Shriji Maharaj has said that one who has become a friend of devotees has become my very life. For this, dharma and discipline are central. Without dharma and discipline, unity will surely break. There will be quarrels and no happiness. If they are there, there is nothing to say to anyone. Unity grows greatly. So if someone is lax, help and assist others in observing the disciplines, but never see their faults. Keep these two, unity and dharma and discipline, and Shriji, Swami and our Gunatit gurus will be extremely pleased.
Jai Shri Swaminarayan.

After Mahant Swami Maharaj's breakfast, there was talk of the "Swaminarayan Bhashya" written by Bhadreshdas Swami. Bhadreshdas Swami said, "After I write, Shrutiprakash Swami reads through all the writing carefully and also suggests the necessary corrections." He went on, "Actually the commentary on the Brahmasutras was to be written by him (Shrutiprakashdas Swami), because he had done a PhD on it and a great deal of preparation too. But Bapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj) gave the command, and he immediately gave it up!"
While all this was being said, Swamishri suddenly stood up from the bed and held the feet of Shrutiprakashdas Swami, who was standing in front, with both hands!!

Then Swamishri stood up and with great pleasure embraced Shrutiprakashdas Swami. This boundless pleasure was because Shrutiprakashdas Swami, on his guru's command, had given up writing the commentaries himself and put Bhadreshdas Swami forward.

One of Swamishri's favourite sayings is: "If, on seeing one sadhu being honoured, another sadhu does not feel envy and is greatly delighted in his mind, he should be known as the crest jewel among all sadhus."

Then, as was his daily habit, Swamishri signalled to the attendant sadhus, "Take out the hearing aids." But when his fingers reached his ears, it turned out the hearing aids were not there at all. Everyone burst out laughing and said, "Swami! You heard without the hearing aids?"
Swamishri laughed and began nodding yes.
The attendant sadhu said, "One hears what one wants to hear."
Atmaswarupdas Swami said, "Swami has been caught."
The senses are a product of maya, while the Satpurush is beyond maya. If the Satpurush does not need the senses to hear, how would he need hearing aids!
After finishing his walk, as Mahant Swami Maharaj was finally sitting in a chair resting, he casually asked Vednayandas Swami, "Have you had an operation?"
Vednayandas Swami said, "Yes, for appendicitis."
Everyone was amazed: how did Swamishri know? But Swamishri had noticed a small scar on Vednayandas Swami's stomach. From that he caught that he had had an operation.
So subtle is Swamishri's power of observation!
